review_scope: Fresh manual inspection of the eight candidate PNGs listed in supplemental-13.input.json, without independent reference PNGs. Settings requirements were checked against DESIGN_HANDOFF.md, phase3-reference-scope.json, phase3-prototype-reference-support.json, and the original handoff and relevant static prototype text.

provenance.candidate_identity: All eight case metadata records identify this run, binary, source, pw5 profile, settings route, and desktop capture backend.
provenance.png_hashes: Get-FileHash SHA256 values for all eight current candidate PNGs match both the input expected_png_sha256 values and the case metadata evidence_hashes.screenshot.sha256 values.
provenance.mechanical_checks: The recorded case checks have no failed entries. These records establish capture identity and declared state, and were not used as a substitute for manual visual inspection.

observations: The dedicated Downloads page has a labeled Settings back action, a large serif title, the active Settings dock, and no root-list pager.
All four read-ahead choices and both persistence switches are visibly disabled. The read-ahead group explicitly identifies its unavailable state instead of claiming an active feature.
The Save location row is populated from the actual case data directory, and the Download management action remains fully visible.

The destination value ends in an ellipsis before the case-specific directory and final demo component. The read-only row has no visible expansion or full-path action, so this page does not let the user identify the full destination.
intentional_differences: Unavailable download integration is accepted as the declared application state.
The real capture data directory may differ from the prototype example destination; that data difference does not excuse truncating the usable destination.

observations: Page 1 contains the version caption, serif Settings title, white outlined Paperwhite 5 card, four device rows, and three reading rows.

The seven visible setting rows match the recorded visible_setting_ids. Their labels and trailing summaries fit without overlap, and the selected profile correctly describes warmth support and no gravity sensor.
The folio reads 1 / 2 with the previous action hidden, the center retained, and the next action at the right edge. The Settings dock remains flush at the bottom.
The card and list use white surfaces, thin separators, and readable grayscale hierarchy without a shadow or dimmed layer.
Brightness 12 and warmth 8 are clearly associated with separate horizontal tracks, square thumbs, and large minus/plus controls.
The brightness thumb is near the midpoint and warmth near one third of the track, consistent with the declared 0..24 control range and current preference values.
The runtime declaration exposes both frontlight and warmth, which supports displaying both controls. No unsupported automatic-brightness or orientation-sensor control appears.
The content has generous separation, remains above the dock, and retains the required labeled back action without a root pager.
intentional_differences: Current brightness and warmth values come from the captured application preferences rather than prototype sample values.
The capture exposes implemented controls on a desktop backend and does not qualify physical light hardware.

observations: All five contrast choices fit in one row. Standard is distinctly selected with black fill and white text, matching contrast 0.
Crop borders and 16-level grayscale dither have active black tracks and right-aligned white knobs, matching the recorded crop_borders and dither preferences.
The dither label does not claim hardware dithering. This agrees with software_dither=true and hardware_dither_qualified=false.
Split spread is visibly disabled rather than shown as an active operation. All three rows and separators remain readable and within the page.
intentional_differences: Unavailable image-processing integration may remain disabled as declared.
The enabled dither control represents the implemented software path rather than unsupported hardware dithering.

observations: Four language rows are evenly separated and fully visible.
Simplified Chinese is bold and has a trailing checkmark at the far right, preserving the required current-language indication.
Traditional Chinese, English, and Japanese are visibly muted, so the screenshot does not suggest those unavailable translations are selected or enabled.
The language list retains the labeled Settings back action and active dock without an unnecessary list pager or clipped row.
intentional_differences: Unavailable translations are accepted as the application's actual state; the screenshot does not simulate a successful language change.

observations: The second root page omits the first-page device card and fits all nine settings rows in Library, Sources and data, and General groups.
The visible rows match categories, auto-update, source-lists, downloads, tracking, backup, language, logs, and about in the captured state.
The folio reads 2 / 2, shows the previous action at the left, preserves the centered page count, and hides the next action at the final boundary.
Unavailable summaries for automatic updates, backup, and logs, the unconfigured tracking summary, and the selected language remain readable without colliding with chevrons.
The page contains the required logfile switch and separate Export logs and Clear logs buttons, all visibly disabled.
No success, log file, or cleanup result is fabricated in the captured state.
The metadata records a nonempty unavailable settings_status, but the page renders no availability message or explanation near the disabled controls.
The disabled controls occupy a small area below the title, leaving enough clear space for a concise status message without clipping or changing the dock.
intentional_differences: Unavailable logging integration is accepted as real application state.
That intentional capability difference does not explain why the recorded unavailable status is omitted from the visible secondary page.

observations: The empty list is represented by a dash rather than a fabricated sample source list or URL, consistent with the zero-list state.
Add source list and Open source management are fully visible side by side, with the labeled back action and active Settings dock retained.
Both actions use the same solid black outline. The Add source list action therefore loses the dashed creation-action treatment explicitly declared by the handoff and source-list prototype.
No shadow, gray backdrop, inaccessible bottom content, or unnecessary root pager is visible.
intentional_differences: Zero stored source lists legitimately replaces the prototype sample list card.
The empty-data difference does not account for the Add source list border-style mismatch.

suggestions.description: The actual download destination is truncated before its identifying directory components, with no visible way to reveal the complete path.
evidence: In the candidate PNG, the Save location value is a single line ending in an ellipsis after the shared run-directory prefix.
case_metadata.state.settings_details contains the complete destination /tmp/aidoku-phase3-ui-round-1/data/a1baf3fe3dc2/pw5--settings-downloads/demo, with enabled=false and no action id.

DESIGN_HANDOFF.md Settings and original HANDOFF.md section 5.7 require a download destination; phase3-reference-scope.json capabilityBounds.data explicitly keeps clipping in scope despite real data differences.
suggestions.recommendation: Wrap the actual destination onto a dedicated multiline value area, or provide a visible full-path detail action that exposes the complete destination on Paperwhite.

suggestions.description: The logging secondary page offers only disabled controls and does not display its recorded unavailable status or explain the current limitation.
evidence: The candidate shows a disabled logfile switch and disabled Export logs and Clear logs buttons, with no inline status text anywhere below the title.
case_metadata.state.settings_status contains a nonempty unavailable message.
phase3-reference-scope.json precedence.real-state and sharedContract.behavior require truthful operation states; the status is available in the evidence but absent from the user-visible page.
suggestions.recommendation: Render the actual unavailable status beside or above the disabled logging actions and include a concise reason where known, so users can understand the current feature state.

suggestions.description: Add source list uses a solid border instead of the handoff's dashed creation-action border.
evidence: The candidate renders Add source list and Open source management with matching solid black outlines.
Original HANDOFF.md section 4.5 specifies a 1.5-pixel dashed outline for creation actions, including Add source list.
prototype/sc-settings.dc.html:271 maps the dashed argument to a dashed line; line 341 sets that argument to true for Add source list and leaves Open source management solid.
suggestions.recommendation: Use the declared white dashed-outline creation-button treatment for Add source list while keeping the management action's solid outline.

limitations: Only the eight input-listed candidate PNGs were opened with view_image. No independent reference PNGs or other candidate images were loaded.
The relevant handoff, scope, prototype support map, and original prototype were read as static text only. The prototype was not executed.

These are 618x824 native desktop captures using the pw5 design profile. Their declared physical reference scale does not qualify an actual Paperwhite panel, frontlight, warmth, sensor, hardware dithering, or pen.

Static screenshots show current values and disabled appearance but do not establish control activation, the 0 and 24 endpoint behavior, persistence, route execution, source-list operations, filesystem effects, or cleanup feedback.

No application, build, tests, validation suite, smoke test, or runtime probe was launched locally or remotely by this reviewer. Existing JSON/text/PNG evidence and allowed SHA256 file reads were used.
No conclusion about physical sleep/wake, retained artwork, 512 MiB operation, performance timing, or the complete phase-three review matrix is possible from this batch.
This batch result does not establish a complete clean round.
